result.overall: The judicial review application is dismissed because the Refugee Protection Division's decision that state protection was available and effective in Korea was reasonable and not patently unreasonable.

themes.name: State protection availability and effectiveness
themes.summary: The decision focuses on whether state protection for abused women in Korea is available and effective, considering both structural presence and practical functioning.

themes.name: Applicant's failure to seek state protection
themes.summary: The Applicant's subjective reluctance and failure to seek state protection despite abuse is considered insufficient to establish lack of protection.

themes.name: Standard of review - patent unreasonableness
themes.summary: The court applies a patent unreasonableness standard to the RPD's assessment of state protection and finds the decision reasonable.

arguments.quote: The Applicant argues that it was reasonable for her, given her particular situation, not to seek state protection.
arguments.claim: It was reasonable for her, given her particular situation, not to seek state protection.

arguments.quote: The Applicant says that the societal values and the shame of accusing a husband of abuse, her emotional dependence on her husband, and, her loneliness in Korea are all factors which make her failure to seek state protection reasonable.
arguments.claim: The societal values and the shame of accusing a husband of abuse, her emotional dependence on her husband, and her loneliness in Korea are all factors which make her failure to seek state protection reasonable.

arguments.quote: The Applicant further says that the RPD failed to consider whether state protection was effective in Korea.
arguments.claim: The RPD failed to consider whether state protection was effective in Korea.

arguments.quote: The Applicant says that the RPD's error was to consider whether organizational structures were in place to the exclusion of considering whether those structures functioned properly.
arguments.claim: The RPD's error was to consider whether organizational structures were in place to the exclusion of considering whether those structures functioned properly.

arguments.quote: In this case, the Applicant never sought any aspect of state protection, even when her mother came to her physical and emotional aid.
arguments.claim: The Applicant never sought any aspect of state protection, even when her mother came to her physical and emotional aid.

arguments.quote: The RPD took account of the state structure for the protection of abused women; it considered the U.S. DOS reports which referred to some problems in executing on the policies of increased protection for abused women.
arguments.claim: The RPD took account of the state structure for the protection of abused women and considered U.S. DOS reports noting some problems in executing policies of increased protection for abused women.

holdings.quote: Ms. Eun Mee Kim (Applicant) was found not to be a refugee or a person in need of protection by the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) of the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB). This is her judicial review of that decision.
holdings.statement: Ms. Eun Mee Kim is the Applicant who was found not to be a refugee or a person in need of protection by the Refugee Protection Division (RPD).

holdings.quote: The Applicant, a female citizen of the Republic of Korea, who is joined in her claim by her 9 year old daughter Inn Woo Cho, bases her claim on spousal abuse. She claims that state protection is not available to her.
holdings.statement: The Applicant is a female citizen of the Republic of Korea who bases her claim on spousal abuse and claims state protection is not available to her.

holdings.quote: The Applicant has a mother and her only sibling living in Canada. As a result, she claims that following their departure to Canada, she became emotionally dependent on Jong Kook Cho. They married in 1995.
holdings.statement: The Applicant has a mother and one sibling living in Canada and became emotionally dependent on her husband after their departure to Canada; they married in 1995.

holdings.quote: She claims that her husband was verbally and psychologically abusive towards her from the very beginning of their marriage. She was physically assaulted and threatened at various times with either a hammer or with a knife.
holdings.statement: The Applicant claims her husband was verbally and psychologically abusive from the start of their marriage and that she was physically assaulted and threatened with a hammer or knife at various times.

holdings.quote: The Applicant said that she told no one about the incidents because of her personal shame and because of the societal stigma attached to such claims. It was only in 2003, when her mother visited her, that the abuse came out in the open. Her mother took charge of the situation, obtained emotional counselling for the Applicant and moved her and her daughter to Canada.
holdings.statement: The Applicant did not tell anyone about the abuse due to personal shame and societal stigma; the abuse only became known in 2003 when her mother visited and took charge of the situation.

holdings.quote: At no time between 1995 and 2003, despite the physical and psychological abuse, did the Applicant seek state protection.
holdings.statement: Between 1995 and 2003, despite the abuse, the Applicant did not seek state protection.

holdings.quote: The burden of establishing that state protection is either non-existent or inadequate rests with the Applicant.
holdings.statement: The burden of establishing that state protection is either non-existent or inadequate rests with the Applicant.

holdings.quote: There is a presumption in favour of the existence of state protection.
holdings.statement: There is a presumption in favour of the existence of state protection.

holdings.quote: An Applicant's subjective reluctance to engage the state in providing protection is not a sufficient basis to conclude that state protection is not available or effective.
holdings.statement: An Applicant's subjective reluctance to engage the state in providing protection is not a sufficient basis to conclude that state protection is not available or effective.

holdings.quote: The standard of review on state protection is patent unreasonableness.
holdings.statement: The standard of review on state protection is patent unreasonableness.

holdings.quote: The RPD's decision, read as a whole, is a reasonable and balanced decision.
holdings.statement: The RPD's decision, read as a whole, is a reasonable and balanced decision.

holdings.quote: It would be unreasonable to suggest that the RPD must conduct a full review of the effectiveness of state protection in Korea (even if that were possible) in the absence of significant evidence of its ineffectiveness.
holdings.statement: It would be unreasonable to require the RPD to conduct a full review of the effectiveness of state protection in Korea without significant evidence of its ineffectiveness.

holdings.quote: There is nothing to suggest that Korea's state protection is a sham or an exercise of "form over substance".
holdings.statement: There is no suggestion that Korea's state protection is a sham or merely an exercise of form over substance.

holdings.quote: Therefore, despite counsel's persuasive efforts, this Court can find no basis upon which to intervene in this decision.
holdings.statement: This Court finds no basis to intervene in the decision below despite counsel's persuasive efforts.

holdings.quote: This application for judicial review will be dismissed.
holdings.statement: The application for judicial review is dismissed.

authorities.quote: (See; Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration) v. Ward (1993), 103 D.L.R.(4th)).
authorities.authority: The presumption and burden of proof regarding state protection are supported by Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration) v. Ward (1993), 103 D.L.R.(4th).
